column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/cargo-publish-each-member-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS PINS. The workflow has exactly ONE job (`release`) and exactly ONE
# job-level condition: `github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'`. So there is one
# real axis of selection — bot vs human — and everything else this table
# declares is pinned deliberately as a NEGATIVE: to record which inputs do NOT
# move the selection, so a future edit that makes one of them matter shows up as
# a diff here instead of as a silent behaviour change.
# WHY IT EXISTS — and the finding it records. This file is part of the sweep
# opened by graphql-synthesizer on 2026-08-08: a release workflow reported
# SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, published nothing, and nothing said so,
# because its ship job carried `&& !github.event.repository.private`. Every
# `*-auto-release*.yml` in substrate carries a `repository.private` guard, so
# each was swept for that silent-no-publish shape.
# THIS WORKFLOW DOES NOT HAVE THAT SHAPE, AND THE INVERSE IS THE POINT.
# Its single `github.event.repository.private` occurrence is in `runs-on`:
#   runs-on: ${{ github.event.repository.private && 'camelot-builder-pleme-eks' || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
# which selects a RUNNER LABEL (a reusable workflow's runs-on bills the CALLER,
# so a metered label here charges every private consumer). It is NOT a publish
# guard, and neither the job nor the composite action it calls
# (pleme-io/actions/cargo-publish-each-member — checked 2026-08-17, no privacy
# guard in action.yml or run.tlisp) gates publication on repo visibility.
# CONSEQUENCE: a PRIVATE caller of this reusable workflow DOES publish to
# crates.io. Rows `public-human-push` and `private-human-push-STILL-PUBLISHES`
# assert exactly that, identical selection on both, so the divergence from
# cargo-auto-release.yml's posture is written down rather than inferred. If a
# privacy guard is ever added to this workflow, the private row must flip to
# expect-skip in the SAME commit — that flip is the whole review signal.
# NO no-bump ROW, deliberately. The bump/skip-when-no-source-changes decision
# lives inside the composite action's steps, per workspace member, and is
# invisible to job selection: no `needs.*.outputs.bumped` exists to model. A
# fabricated no-bump row would assert nothing and read as coverage. The
# `skip-when-no-source-changes` axis is unassertable at this layer — see the
# workflow's own inputs.
# always() is supplied per case even though no condition reads it, so a rerun
# posture is expressible the day a second job (needs-propagating) lands.
# Baseline: a human push on a PUBLIC repo. The one job runs and publishes.
public-human-push
# THE ROW WORTH READING. Same selection as the public row, on purpose: private
# repos publish through this workflow. Not a bug and not an oversight in the
# table — it is the measured posture, asserted so a change to it cannot be
# silent. Contrast cargo-auto-release.yml, whose ship job skips here.
private-human-push-STILL-PUBLISHES
# The loop guard: the action pushes per-member tags, a tag push re-triggers the
# caller, and the bot must not publish again. This is the workflow's only real
# selection decision.
bot-actor-no-publish-loop
# Same guard on a private repo — the actor check is visibility-independent.
bot-actor-private-no-publish-loop
# A non-push trigger (a caller wiring this to workflow_dispatch or schedule)
# changes nothing: event_name is pinned as a negative, per the header.
human-dispatch-still-runs
